# Research Ops

Curated by Skill Harbor: Research Ops, the operator wrapper around the ECC research stack, for when you want fresh facts, comparisons, enrichment, or recommendations built from current public evidence. It is explicit that it does not replace deep-research, exa-search, or market-research: it tells you when and how to use them together. The workflow starts from what the user already supplied, normalizing it into already-evidenced facts, needs verification, and open questions, instead of restarting analysis from zero. Then it classifies the ask into one of four lanes, quick factual answer, comparison or decision memo, lead or enrichment pass, or recurring monitoring candidate, and takes the lightest useful evidence path first: exa-search for fast discovery, deep-research when multi-source synthesis matters, market-research when the outcome should end in a recommendation, lead-intelligence when the real ask is target ranking. Guardrails are the point: never answer current questions from stale memory when fresh search is cheap, and always separate sourced facts from user-provided evidence, inference, and recommendation. The output format is fixed with QUESTION TYPE, EVIDENCE, INFERENCE, and RECOMMENDATION sections, freshness-sensitive answers carry concrete dates, and the workflow ends by deciding whether the task should become a monitor instead of a repeated manual search. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest...
